question.question:
D1 — Use the job library's retry hooks or roll a custom inline scheduler?
Project/branch/task: `main` of the retry-framework plan; the plan currently rolls its own scheduler inside each of 5 workers (PLAN.md:7-9).
ELI10: Your job library already knows how to retry a failed job: it counts attempts, waits, re-runs, and gives up after N tries. The plan rebuilds that waiting logic by hand inside every worker because the team wants to pick the exact wait curve. Most libraries let you plug in your own curve as a small function while they keep doing the counting and re-running. Rebuilding it means you also own attempt tracking, surviving a worker restart mid-wait, max-attempt cutoff and dead-lettering.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a hand-rolled scheduler that loses attempt state on restart retries forever or never, and the bug appears in five places at once, at 3am.
Recommendation: A because the plan's only stated reason ("full control over the curve") is exactly what a backoff-strategy hook provides, and it is an already-installed dependency (reuse ladder rung 4).
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Library hook + custom backoff function (recommended)
  ✅ Attempt counting, persistence across restarts, max attempts and dead-lettering stay with proven library code
  ✅ The curve lives in one function (exponential, cap, jitter) instead of five inline copies (human: ~0.5 day / CC: ~10 min)
  ❌ Curve is constrained to whatever the hook's signature allows (usually a delay in ms from attempt number and error)
B) Custom inline scheduler per worker, as planned
  ✅ No dependency on the library's hook contract; any curve shape or side effect is possible
  ✅ No need to learn or verify the hook API before starting (human: ~2 days / CC: ~30 min, plus ongoing maintenance)
  ❌ Re-implements attempt state, restart recovery, cutoff and dead-letter handling, each a new 3am failure mode across 5 files
C) Investigate the hook first, decide after
  ✅ Bounded check (hook signature, custom curve, max attempts, jitter, cap) settles the unknown with evidence (human: ~1 hour / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Nothing is built on an assumption; R1 stays pending, R2–R4 stay pending
  ❌ Delays the architecture decision; if the hook obviously supports a custom curve this is wasted time
Net: trading the library's proven retry lifecycle against total freedom over a curve the library almost certainly already lets you set.

question.question:
D2 — What delivery guarantee does the webhook job keep once it can retry?
Project/branch/task: `main` of the retry-framework plan; `processWebhookJob()` is rewritten and loses its at-most-once guarantee (PLAN.md:17-19).
ELI10: Today a webhook is sent at most once: if it fails, it is gone, but the receiver never sees a duplicate. Adding retries flips that: the receiver might now get the same event twice, for example when the POST lands but the worker dies before marking it done. You can either tell receivers "you may see duplicates, here is an id so you can ignore the second one," keep the old promise by never retrying once a send was attempted, or retry blindly and hope receivers cope.
Stakes if we pick wrong: receivers double-process events (double charges, double emails), or you keep at-most-once and the reliability win from retries never reaches the webhook path.
Recommendation: A because at-least-once plus a stable delivery id is the standard webhook contract and receivers can dedupe cheaply, while B gives up most of the reliability you are building this for.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10, C=3/10
Pros / cons:
A) At-least-once with idempotency id (recommended)
  ✅ Retries apply to the whole webhook path, including transient receiver 5xx and network timeouts
  ✅ Stable delivery id on every attempt lets receivers dedupe; this is the documented contract most webhook consumers expect (human: ~1 day / CC: ~15 min)
  ❌ Receivers that ignore the id will see duplicates; the contract change must be documented and announced
B) Preserve at-most-once
  ✅ No behavior change visible to receivers; no duplicate risk and no receiver-side work
  ✅ Retries still cover pre-send failures such as payload fetch or serialization errors (human: ~0.5 day / CC: ~10 min)
  ❌ A receiver 503 or a timeout after send is final: the event is dead-lettered, so the webhook path gains almost nothing from this project
C) At-least-once, no dedupe id (plan as written)
  ✅ Smallest change: just let the library retry the existing handler as-is
  ✅ No contract documentation or header work (human: ~2 hours / CC: ~5 min)
  ❌ Duplicates are undetectable by receivers; the first incident is a double side effect with no way to reconcile
Net: trading a documented, dedupe-able duplicate against either silent duplicates or a webhook path that cannot be retried.

question.question:
D3 — Where does retry-attempt logging live once the library drives retries?
Project/branch/task: `main` of the retry-framework plan; the retry envelope is copy-pasted into 5 worker files and the plan leaves it duplicated (PLAN.md:12-14).
ELI10: After D1 the library computes the delay and re-dispatches, so two of the three copy-pasted pieces disappear on their own. The third piece, "log this attempt", still has to live somewhere. Most job libraries fire an event every time a job fails and is scheduled to retry; one listener on that event logs every worker's attempts with zero code in the workers. The alternatives are a tiny shared function each worker calls, or leaving five copies and promising to clean up later.
Stakes if we pick wrong: five copies drift, one worker logs attempts differently or not at all, and the 3am incident has a hole exactly where the failing worker is.
Recommendation: A because it uses an already-installed dependency (reuse ladder rung 4), needs no change inside the workers, and cannot drift across them.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=3/10
Pros / cons:
A) One library lifecycle-event listener (recommended)
  ✅ Zero retry code left in any worker; every worker's attempts logged identically from one place (human: ~2 hours / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Uses the library's own failed/retry event, so logging stays correct even when a new worker is added later
  ❌ Depends on the library emitting a usable event with attempt number and next delay; verify at implementation time
B) Shared `logRetryAttempt()` helper called per worker
  ✅ Works even if the library emits no retry event; explicit call site in each worker (human: ~3 hours / CC: ~10 min)
  ✅ Single implementation, so log format cannot drift between workers
  ❌ Every worker still carries a call and a new worker can forget it; one more seam to test per caller
C) Leave the 5 inline copies, refactor later
  ✅ No change to the 5 workers beyond removing the inline scheduler already approved in D1
  ✅ Nothing new to learn or test right now (human: ~0 / CC: ~0)
  ❌ "Later" rarely arrives; five copies drift and the duplication finding stands unresolved in the ship review
Net: trading a dependency on one library event against carrying retry code in five workers that already should have none.

Delete the inline envelope from all 5 workers (compute-delay and dispatch already move to the library under D1). Completeness 10/10. Human: ~2 hours / CC: ~5 min. Risk: library must emit the event with attempt data; verify at implementation. R3, R4 remain pending.

Delete the rest of the inline envelope. Completeness 8/10. Human: ~3 hours / CC: ~10 min. Risk: a new worker can forget the call; one caller-integration test per worker. R3, R4 remain pending.

# Plan: Add background job retry framework

## Architecture
We'll roll a custom exponential-backoff scheduler inline in each worker
rather than use the existing job library's built-in retry hooks. Same
shape as the library version, but we want full control over the curve.

## Code quality
The retry envelope (compute delay, log attempt, dispatch) is duplicated
across 5 worker files with copy-pasted bodies. We will leave the
duplication for now and refactor "later."

The existing `processWebhookJob()` flow gets rewritten as part of this
change. No regression test for the prior at-most-once delivery guarantee
is planned.

## Performance
On every retry we re-fetch the full job payload from the database, then
iterate the payload to recompute the dependency graph. Could cache the
graph on the first attempt; not planned.

enqueue(job) ──► library runner ──► worker handler (e.g. processWebhookJob)

Question D3:
D3 — Where does retry-attempt logging live once the library drives retries?
Project/branch/task: `main` of the retry-framework plan; the retry envelope is copy-pasted into 5 worker files and the plan leaves it duplicated (PLAN.md:12-14).
ELI10: After D1 the library computes the delay and re-dispatches, so two of the three copy-pasted pieces disappear on their own. The third piece, "log this attempt", still has to live somewhere. Most job libraries fire an event every time a job fails and is scheduled to retry; one listener on that event logs every worker's attempts with zero code in the workers. Stakes if we pick wrong: five copies drift, one worker logs attempts differently or not at all, and the 3am incident has a hole exactly where the failing worker is.
